payload.title: How Do You Get a Marriage Licence?
payload.h1: How Do You Get a Marriage Licence?
payload.excerpt: If you are searching for a marriage licence in Australia, there is none to apply for. Marry abroad and the destination's law takes over, and some places do issue licences.
key_takeaways: Australia has no marriage licence: the equivalent step is giving a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant between 1 and 18 months before the wedding.

A licence permits a marriage while a certificate records one, and in Australia the certificate that counts is the official copy from the state or territory registry, not the ceremonial one signed on the day.
New Zealand and Hawaii issue marriage licences through their own authorities, each with its own timing rules.
The decision that shapes everything else is which country makes your marriage legal: Australia, with a symbolic ceremony abroad, or your destination, under its own law.

faq.q: Do you need a marriage licence to get married in Australia?
faq.a: No. As at November 2026, you give a notice of intended marriage to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding, under [the Attorney-General's Department guidance](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married).

faq.q: What is the difference between a marriage licence and a marriage certificate?
faq.a: A licence permits a marriage and a certificate shows that a legal marriage has been performed, as the Hawaii State Department of Health explains. In Australia there is no licence, and the certificate you need to change your name or prove your marriage is the official one from the registry.

faq.q: How do you register your marriage in Australia?
faq.a: Your celebrant submits the paperwork to the registry in the state or territory where you married within 14 days of the wedding. You then apply to the registry for the official certificate, or ask your celebrant to apply for you.

faq.q: What makes a marriage valid in Australia?
faq.a: As at November 2026, you must not already be married, not be marrying a parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, brother or sister, and be at least 18 (unless a court has approved a marriage where 1 person is 16 to 18). You must also understand what marriage means, agree to marry voluntarily and use specific words in the ceremony.

faq.q: Can you get married without witnesses?
faq.a: Not in Australia. Two witnesses aged over 18 sign the marriage certificates, and the celebrant must be physically present with you and the witnesses. Overseas, ask the destination's embassy or consulate.

faq.q: Is a marriage licence from New Zealand or Hawaii recognised in Australia?
faq.a: What is recognised is the marriage, not the licence. [An overseas marriage](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/planning-trip/advice-your-planned-activities/getting-married-overseas) is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law. It cannot be registered here.
